title: Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter
summary: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents has entered private beta, extending self-hosting beyond sandboxes to the harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history, which can all run in your cloud or on-prem. Model routing can go to Anthropic, Bedrock, Google Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or your own gateway, and session history stays in your database (ZDR applies if your org has it). Security features include separating code from the agent loop and secrets, allowlisted network hosts, and OpenTelemetry export.

title: Your apps can now open in Claude, and Claude can work in them
summary: Partner apps can now open inside Claude beside chat or full screen, built on the open MCP Apps extension, and Claude can edit open pages, rows, and files with user approval for actions. It is rolling out on web and desktop to all plans, starting with Asana, Canva, and Notion, and admins can restrict connector tools as they do today. Developers can also run full apps inside Claude in public preview.

title: Introducing Claude for Manufacturing
summary: Anthropic released a manufacturing plugin with 17 skills and four connectors (Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365, and Oracle NetSuite) covering quotes, failed-inspection investigation, breakdown diagnosis, supplier sourcing, design comparison, and production reports. Infor is releasing its own plugin so Claude can act, such as releasing POs or rescheduling production, after user approval. Humans review anything before it reaches customers or suppliers, and the plugin targets manual data work affecting 79% of manufacturers on Team and Enterprise plans.

title: More ways to work with Claude: Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors
summary: New artifact types include Claude Sheets (collaborative spreadsheets with formulas and tabs), Whiteboards, and Claude Data (formerly Dashboards), which connects to tools like Snowflake and Salesforce to build dashboards. Partner apps such as Adobe and Atlassian can run inside Claude, and Claude Meetings is coming soon. These tools let non-technical teams build tools and move ideas across formats with shared context, while working within existing permissions that admins control.

title: The Claude Tag guide for startups
summary: A guide shows how eight startups use Claude Tag (beta), which lets teams @mention Claude in Slack to run tasks with connected tools, across five setups: on-call triage, threads to draft PRs, a company brain, self-serve data analysis, and recurring reports. Campfire went from mention to open PR in 21 minutes, and Moritz cut a daily update from about an hour to 5 minutes. The advice is to start with one task in a small private pilot, limit access, and have humans review and merge PRs, with Claude Tag available on Beta, Team, and Enterprise plans.

title: Building always-on agents
summary: Anthropic published a guide to stateful, proactive agents that sleep and wake for brief runs to handle events, built around five primitives: event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and outbox. Interest is renewed as models judge intent and timing better and long-horizon work gets cheaper, citing a 78% cost drop per solved task from Opus 5 to Opus 5.5. It recommends safeguards such as credential proxies, deferred approvals, and tuning message frequency, and gives developers a blueprint for adding proactive agents to products.
